approved: Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill 2013

Moved a bill requiring the Parliamentary Budget Office to publish a post-election report costing every political party's election commitments within 30 days of a new government forming, covering parties with five or more members or senators, and allowing the ATO to share confidential taxpayer data with the office.

Supported the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill 2013, which would add post-election costings and reporting functions, information-gathering powers and access to protected taxpayer information, while criticising the government's handling of amendments to its own amendments.

Supported the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill 2013, arguing that post-election assessment would promote costed policies and scrutiny, including where parties avoided the Charter of Budget Honesty, and criticising claims about Treasury's role in assessing a stated $70 billion gap.

Supported the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill 2013, arguing that the PBO would provide common assumptions for costings, assess election commitments, and allow parties 48 hours to respond to its post-election report.

Summed up debate on the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill, arguing its post-election costing report will hold political parties accountable for uncosted election promises, and thanked the opposition for supporting the bill and forthcoming amendments.

The Coalition supported the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Bill 2013, which gives the Parliamentary Budget Office the additional function of auditing election costings for all parties and preparing a report within 30 days after a government is formed. The speaker argued this ensures all parties are honest in their policy commitments and that policies are fully and accurately costed.
Parliamentary Service Amendment (Parliamentary Budget Officer) Act 2013
